top_categories.workout_context: 80ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Dragon Ride L'Etape Wales' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
At mile 60 of 143, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
At Dragon Ride L'Etape Wales, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.

Road-specific control matters at Dragon Ride L'Etape Wales. Practice on paved Welsh mountain roads through the Brecon: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 143 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Dragon Ride L'Etape Wales. Train it until it feels boring.
11,483ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
11,483ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 11,483ft of climbing on paved Welsh mountain roads through the Brecon does to your power file on race day.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Dragon Ride L'Etape Wales. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Low-cadence force work supports 11,483ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on paved Welsh mountain roads through the Brecon can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Dragon Ride L'Etape Wales’s 143 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Dragon Ride L'Etape Wales rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on paved welsh mountain roads through the brecon beacons national park to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and Durability to prepare you for 143 miles of paved welsh mountain roads through the brecon beacons national park in Margam Park, Port Talbot, South Wales, UK.
